solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old president in uniform following ceremony I perform

indicators.note: the uniform letter is placed after the rest, coming next in line

parts.note: pomp is stately ceremonial display
taken as written
to do is to perform, as in doing a play
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A former head of state in dress uniform takes part in some state ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Pompidou was President of France from 1969 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompidou is a past French head of state, so an example of an old president.

clue.text: Bomb may not be if it has this

definitions.meaning: the clue reads straight on into the answer, saying a bomb may be serviceable or not
the answer split another way gives a round letter for nothing next to a detonating cord: having nothing of that kind

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as OF USE completing the sentence, and also as O FUSE, nought fuse: a bomb with no fuse won't go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of use is serviceable, and a bomb lacking any detonator serves no purpose at all.

clue.text: The blessed Guardian's not partisan, somehow!

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are put together in an unspecified new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A neutral claim that the Guardian newspaper takes no political side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian looks like the newspaper, but the guardian here is a protecting saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron saint is a holy figure regarded as the special protector of a place, trade or person.

clue.text: Sharing out reward, ultimately two pairs in contention?

indicators.note: in the end, so only the final letter of reward is used

parts.note: its last letter is taken
two pairs make four, IV in Roman numerals
vying means competing, in contention with others

explanation.surface: Splitting a prize when two couples are tied in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To divvy up is an informal way of saying to divide or share out among people.

clue.text: Inside out? Stick with solution

parts.note: someone out cold under anaesthetic is said to be under
to lock is to stick fast, as jammed wheels lock
and joins one thing with another
a key is the solution to a puzzle, as with an answer key

explanation.surface: A puzzled 'inside out?' answered by advice to stick with the solution you have.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside is slang for in prison, where a convict is kept securely shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept under lock and key means being locked up, which is what being inside, in jail, means.

clue.text: Preserve item, often mechanical, a source of drama

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hard fruit usually made into jelly or jam
second meaning: Peter ..., the carpenter among Shakespeare's 'rude mechanicals' who writes and directs their play

explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream the working men are called mechanicals, and Quince is the one who produces the play within the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a fruit seldom eaten raw and commonly made into jelly or membrillo; Quince is also the mechanicals' playwright.

clue.text: Filling in cheque, as you've not settled?

indicators.note: the answer fills the inside of these words, sitting within them

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone uneasy filling in a cheque for a bill still unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' suggests payment of the cheque, but here it means calm in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy is having an unsettled, nauseous stomach, or being uneasy.

clue.text: Maybe poverty's rise in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End are known for dropping their aitches

parts.note: a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A remark that poverty is increasing in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class Cockney district of London, whose speakers drop the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill is a misfortune or evil, and poverty is an example of such a social ill.

clue.text: Don cape before a dance, leading lady love

indicators.note: the cape letter comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
taken as written
a ball is a formal dance
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the queen, the first lady of the land
love is zero in tennis, a round O

explanation.surface: Putting on a cape before a dance, with a lady love in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a verb meaning put on, but it is the Spanish title for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman or knight, and Don is the Spanish honorific for such a man.

clue.text: Maybe Swede's boss informally embracing celebrity, mostly

indicators.note: the boss word holds the other piece in its arms, around it

parts.note: guv is a casual term for a boss or governor

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A Swedish worker's manager cosying up to someone famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Several kings of Sweden have been named Gustav, so a Gustav is one example of a Swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav is a common Swedish man's name, borne by several Swedish kings, so it exemplifies a Swede.

clue.text: Unusual label on jacket accompanying a cloak

indicators.note: one thing on another follows it here, so the rearranged label comes after the jacket

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unusual, not normal, order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd tag on a jacket worn together with a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit after the jacket abbreviation, as if a label was put on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A djellaba is a loose hooded robe or cloak worn in North Africa.

clue.text: Love last traces of jazz age ever so

indicators.note: the final remnant of each word, so the last letter of each is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fond nostalgia for the final remnants of the Jazz Age, ever so much loved.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis term for a nil score, meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: Large amounts of alcohol — old fine — introduced to US domestic market

indicators.note: the old fine pieces are put into the market, brought inside it

parts.note: a yard sale is an American sale of household goods held outside a home
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Old, fine beer brought to the American home market in big quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard of ale is a tall glass holding about two and a half pints of beer, traditionally downed in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Yards of ale are tall beer glasses holding a large quantity, so large measures of alcohol.

clue.text: Pay for courses, with books in principle

indicators.note: the books abbreviation goes in, inside the rest

parts.note: to pay for courses at table is to fund a meal
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Paying tuition fees and buying books as a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests education but means the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamental is a basic rule or principle on which other things rest.

clue.text: Spectator originally keen on following race meets

indicators.note: these pieces come after the race word

parts.note: a run is a race

indicators.note: at its origin, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter is used
into is informal for enthusiastic about

explanation.surface: A spectator who is a fan of a race bumps into someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, encountering them unexpectedly.

clue.text: S American revolutionary: more than that, a university teacher

indicators.note: something in revolution turns round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: nay can mean not only that but more, as in 'good, nay excellent'
taken as written
a guru is a spiritual teacher

explanation.surface: A South American rebel who is also an academic lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like part of the definition, a guerrilla perhaps, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uruguayan is a person from Uruguay, a country of South America.

clue.text: A sign November is turning to December time

indicators.note: turning around means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Seasonal talk of November giving way to December.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the festive season falling in December.

clue.text: Place to go after ascending, with endless special food?

definitions.text: Place to go after ascending, with endless special food?

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, the place you go to

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hallah (challah) is the plaited bread eaten on the Jewish Sabbath and festivals

explanation.surface: A heavenly destination after ascending, complete with feasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Valhalla, the Norse hall slain warriors rise to after death, where they feast endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Valhalla is the hall of Odin where heroes slain in battle go after death to feast for ever.

clue.text: Mountain republic's more westerly one excavated for uranium

indicators.note: dug out and swapped for, so one letter is removed and another put in its place

parts.note: Fiji is a Pacific island republic
the left-hand I, as west is left on a map
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A mountain in a republic being mined for its uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two letters I in the republic, the more westerly is the left-hand one, since across entries read west to east.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuji is Japan's highest peak, the volcanic mountain Mount Fuji.

clue.text: Briefly take old vessel back round a volcanic island

indicators.note: going back means these pieces are read in reverse
cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: its last letter is dropped
Noah's Ark is the ancient ship of Genesis
a round shape is the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick instruction to sail an ancient boat back around something.
explanation.walkthrough: Krakatoa is the Indonesian volcano whose 1883 eruption was one of the most violent recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakatoa is an island volcano in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra.

clue.text: Woman's who's fallen — case of fuel leaking?

indicators.note: the outside, its first and last letters, holds the word like a case

parts.note: its outer letters are taken
oozy means seeping, oozing liquid

explanation.surface: A woman fallen ill from a fuel leak.
explanation.walkthrough: A fallen woman is an old phrase for one considered of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A floozy is a disreputable woman of loose morals, what was once called a fallen woman.

clue.text: Cuckoo with intention of feeding?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crazy, not in one's right mind
second meaning: gone off for a midday meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' tempts towards the bird and its habit of laying eggs in others' nests for feeding, but here it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mentally absent or crazy, and literally describes someone away having a meal.

clue.text: Old version of my commercial — as before

indicators.note: this piece comes ahead of the other

parts.note: eg, for example, can stand in for as in 'fruits such as apples'
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: An advertiser rerunning an old version of their commercial, the same as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is a dated oath of surprise, an archaic equivalent of the exclamation 'my!'.

clue.text: Spent, having nothing else to pay?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: inclusive of every charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like a word about money, which the second half encourages, but it means tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in is British slang for exhausted, and an all-in price covers every cost with no extras.

clue.text: What boy working with monk after hours produces?

definitions.text: What boy working with monk after hours produces?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the hours letter
the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choirboy and a monk at evening office pull out the book of hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the scene: a choirboy and a monk at the canonical hours would sing from this.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnbook is a collection of hymns that a chorister and a monk would use at services.

clue.text: Called before match not being broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, not

explanation.surface: A commentator's line about a match not shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The match is a marriage, and née introduces the name a married woman was born with.
explanation.definitionFit: Née marks a woman's maiden name, what she was called before marrying.

clue.text: Grant airworthiness certificate perhaps, and send out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: allow to take to the air
second meaning: release or hurl a missile or volley of words

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads literally, permitting an aircraft into the air; the second is the idiom for launching a missile or an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is to discharge something forcefully, and literally to permit a plane to go airborne.

clue.text: World body backed agreement to hold vote without it

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is the world organisation

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the vote mark inside it
put in reverse, so read backwards

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The UN supporting a deal to hold a vote without some element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the old slang for sex appeal, so being without it is lacking allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsexy means lacking sexual allure or appeal, the quality once called 'it'.

clue.text: Young creature dying after taking lion's head for its tail!

indicators.note: the longing word takes on a new letter in exchange
the new letter replaces the end letter of the first syllable, yearn

parts.note: dying for something means yearning for it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A dying animal whose tail has been swapped for a lion's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter swapped is the tail of yearn, the first N.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is an animal, especially a horse, in its second year, so a young creature.
